originality.rationale: The explicit rank-eight singular Jacobian and its rank-two kernel for this right Euclidean four-simplex, together with a definite projected quadratic obstruction and sharp inverse Hölder exponent, are absent from the inspected results. Mohar–Rivin prove independence at a regular simplex and give other singular/discrete nonuniqueness examples; Gaifullin treats generic algebraic fibers; Zhang raises the general Euclidean continuous-rigidity question and constructs pseudo-Euclidean deformations. The new theorem is neither a corollary of the regular-point inverse theorem nor a disguised restatement of the known singular-example family. Relevant searches were examined semantically, not treated as proof of novelty.

It distinguishes an integrable infinitesimal deformation from a two-dimensional algebraic infinitesimal kernel that is completely blocked at second order, overcoming the failure of the usual Jacobian inverse argument. This is a natural geometric local-rigidity question with structural obstruction rather than a parameter substitution or a routine numerical invariant.
